Prescribed Assets - Pension Capture?

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What plans does the ANC have for your pension after the elections? Carte Blanche investigates the ANC plan to prescribe assets

Unique Selling Point:
Good graphics to assist in the story telling and good data. Different views to drive the narrative. Excellent consumer story

Summary:
PENSION CAPTURE PROPOSAL

By 2021 South Africa will be R3.5 trillion rand in debt. We are not far off from that right now. Take a look at South Africa’s debt clock run by commodity.com, every second our interest compounding at eye watering figures, faster than one can say Tito Mboweni.

Our interest payments alone cost over R5000 every second, and currently national debt per citizen sits at around R56 000. In economists speak, our debt is around 56% of GDP.

Treasury have not minced their words and things may only stabilize around 5- 6 years from now at 57% of GDP.

GRAPH GOES HERE

The above data shows that this year alone R202 billion rand of our hard- earned money will go just into servicing our debt. It’s a frightening picture because South Africa is broke, and government is struggling to find money to pay its debts. But they have a plan and that plan could directly impact on the money you are saving for your retirement.

ENTER PRESCRIBED ASETTS





Further information:
By 2021 South Africa will be R3.5 trillion rand in debt. We are not far off from that right now. Take a look at South Africa’s debt clock run by commodity.com, every second our interest compounding at eye watering figures, faster than one can say Tito Mboweni.

Our interest payments alone cost over R5000 every second, and currently national debt per citizen sits at around R56 000. In economists speak, our debt is around 56% of GDP.

Treasury have not minced their words and things may only stabilize around 5- 6 years from now at 57% of GDP.



The above data shows that this year alone R202 billion rand of our hard- earned money will go just into servicing our debt. It’s a frightening picture because South Africa is broke, and government is struggling to find money to pay its debts. But they have a plan and that plan could directly impact on the money you are saving for your retirement.

ENTER PRESCRIBED ASETTS

In January this year when the ANC presented their Manifesto, they said the following:

“We will investigate the introduction of prescribed assets on financial institutions funds to unlock resources for investment in social and economic development”

BUT WHAT EXACTLY DOES THAT MEAN?
In a nutshell, it means that when government needs money, (which they do) all they have to do is make it mandatory for fund managers managing any of your savings, to place a percentage of those savings into funds identified by government. In other words, failing State owned assets like Eskom or SAA. Neither you nor your fund manager will have any choice on the matter, and this could have a devastating impact on your pension.

THE HONEY POT
While South Africa may be broke, there is still a large honey pot that till now has been left untouched. Collectively South Africans have R4.3 trillion rand in private pension funds. What is incredible is that we have more in our pension funds than Germany, for example, and are up there with some of the first world countries. This huge pot of money has not gone unnoticed by the ANC. According to economist Mike Schussler whose recent study sounds a dire warning, it will be a lot easier for the government to raid these funds than go to the IMF cap in hand. The IMF will demand transparency and reform, but prescribing assets can be done without even passing new laws. All they need to do is amend regulation 28.

REGULATION 28
Right now, Regulation 28 is there to protect you. It ensures that a fund manager spreads your risk – he can only put 75% of your pension into equities, 25% into local or international property and 30% into foreign investments. But the catch, according to Mike Schussler is that regulation 28 means that should government want to prescribe that your pension goes into a loss- making hole, they don’t even have to change the law, all they need to do is amend regulation 28.

ITS BEEN DONE BEFORE
When the apartheid government was the pariah of the world, they struggled to get access to international finance and forced pension funds to invest in SASOL, ISCOR and various other entities, but abandoned the policy in 1989.

WHO WILL IT AFFECT?
About 11 to 16 million South Africans with pension funds and more if one considers the knock on effect, and according to Schussler’s graphs – it’s mostly black South Africans whose investment in pension funds has increased dramatically, while white pension fund investors have dropped from 70% down to 22%. Coloured and Indian investors have stayed more or less constant.


WHAT EFFECT WILL PRESCRIBING ASETTS HAVE?
Disastrous according to ALF Lees and various other pension fund managers, including economist Thabi Leoka. They say money will pour out of this country. Not so says Mark Barnes, CEO of the post office.


BROKEN PROMISES
The debt burden is huge – add the debts from State owned enterprises and a debt of closer to 100% of GDP is the real story. In 2008 it was 46% of GDP – 11 years later its practically double – and don’t listen to the promises of politicians warns Schussler. They told us that SA will not have a debt to GDP ratio of more than 40%. Oh dear that didn’t last, so the next line in the sand they drew was 50%. Then 60% …oops, we crossed that line too…so what next

FALLING OUT OF THE WORLD BOND INDICES
If that sounds complicated it really isn’t, but one does need to understand how that can impact on you. Currently foreign investors make up nearly 40% of our debt market. But if we continue to mismanage our economy we will most certainly get downgraded again. And there is a limit to these downgrades. At a point portfolio managers will be forced to withdraw their funds that is propping up our debt. That will make our debt more expensive and government will need to issue further bonds and then all they have to do is change the % share of regulation 28 and force fund managers to buy up those bonds. That is the picture Schussler is warning us against.

SO WHAT IS EVERYONE ELSE SAYING?
After the ANC issued its manifesto in January, the pension fund industry was skrikked, but two things happened. An election was announced, and the ANC went silent on the matter. And because there were no further details available, the pension fund industry appeared to stop panicking. In fact, Alexander Forbes chief Economist Isaah Mahlanga said his view was that it was a low probability event. Not so fast, warns ALF LEES, the DA shadow deputy minister who sits on the finance committee in parliament with the ANC. He is convinced that it will come into effect at some point after the elections. Surprisingly the unions are apparently in favour of prescribed assets.

WHAT IS THE PLAN?
There are at least two people in the ruling party who should know – Yunus Carrim chairperson of the finance committee and Enoch Godongwana, head of the ANC economic transformation committee. We will endeavor to get answers from either of these politicians. Let us not forget that Carrim is a communist so nationalizing your pension is not novel to him, it’s just the way he rolls.

SO WHAT DO YOU DO?
Don’t panic say the experts. We will explore in more detail what options are available to investors should prescribed assets become a reality

IS IT CRUNCH TIME?
Yes says Schussler.

FINAL SCRIPT PENSION CAPTURE TX Sunday 5th May 2019.

Commentary One
Imagine a future where the investment of your pension money is not determined by where you can get the best returns, but rather by a government decree, based on their financial needs. This is called prescribed assets and its proposed in the ANC’s latest manifesto.

It says:

We will investigate the introduction of prescribed assets on financial institutions’ funds to unlock resources for investments in social and economic development

LINK
That proposal in the manifesto sent a shiver through the pension fund industry, but perhaps the rest of us didn’t understand how prescribed assets if implemented could devastate the health of our pensions

Commentary Two
Mike Brown is chairman of the investment analysts society. He also runs his own fund.

MIKE BROWN
We were concerned about it because don’t forget the ANC is a socialist government and typically, they tend to try lay their hands on as much of other people’s money as they can.

Commentary Three
At this stage it’s still an ANC resolution, and not yet government policy. Enoch Godongwana is the head of Economic transformation for the party, and was one of the drafters of that resolution

Enoch Godongwana
The resolution says carefully worded that we want to investigate prescribed assets, that is what the resolution says. The reason we have crafted it in that way, is that we don’t implement without clear thinking, on which asset classes, what are the cost to our economy.

Commentary four
Already your pension funds are subject to a softer form of prescription called Regulation 28. This compels your fund manager to spread your investment across several asset classes. Right now, that’s a maximum of 75% in the share market, 30% offshore, 25% in listed properties and as much as you wish in government bonds and cash.

Enoch Godongwana
So for us, we may have to move for an amendment and broadening of regulation 28, if the circumstances after investigation necessitated that



Commentary five courtesy GCIS
All it would take is a minister’s signature to amend Regulation 28, and overnight you could be forced to invest in government assets that may offer little or no return

Mike Brown
Government can change that regulation, it doesn’t need an act of parliament. A regulation can out from the minister of finance can say well now you have to have a much bigger percentage in government bonds. In other words, you must fund the government.
Devi
There is something that is not right about that. I mean morally right
Mike Brown
I don’t think its correct at all! This is just state capture in its next form and hopefully we can stop it happening.

Commentary six
Many of us are not aware that South Africa has one of the biggest pension savings in the world in dollar terms. Economist Mike Schussler has done the research and his numbers show over four trillion rands sitting in our collective pension savings

Mike Schussler
South Africa is the emerging market which has the highest amount of pension assets in the world. There is no emerging market, including China, including Brazil, including Russia that has anywhere close to the savings that South Africa has! South Africa has more pension funds savings than either France or Germany!
Devi
Is that the reason why our pension pot is so sexy because there is all this money sitting there?
Mike
Our pension pot is the sexiest thing for government at the moment. I really think it is likely to happen
Devi
That would be very worrying because I wouldn’t want someone to tell me where to put my money
Mike
Exactly, and your money will not grow as quickly as it should, and you will end up a very poor person if the returns aren’t right. For example, if people told you told to put your money in Eskom Bonds and Eskom cannot pay back
Devi
Not on your life and then what!
Mike
And then you will live in your kids garage if you are old.

Commentary seven
But Enoch Godongwana dismisses this interpretation of their resolution as nonsense.

Enoch
So, you are singling out, deliberately in my view a scarecrow, that the only way we can do prescribed assets is to send it to an SOE, that is not what we are talking about!
Devi
But you are not categorically saying to me that won’t happen?

Enoch Godongwana
I said it won’t happen!
Devi
Guaranteed?
Enoch Godongwana
Guaranteed. It won’t happen
DEVI
Do you blame people for not having trust right now? They don’t trust….
Enoch
I don’t expect people to trust in the environment in which Eskom has performed. But I don’t expect when you talk about prescribed assets, of necessity, you mean we put them in SAA that is not what we are talking about!
Devi
The point I am making is that I don’t trust…
ENOCH
You are not the one who is going to make the decision about prescribed assets
Devi
No I am not, that is for sure!
Enoch
Then you should be listening to me I am the one who is going to make that decision about
prescribed assets

LINK
But Alexander Forbes, who manage one of South Africa’s largest pension funds, is not convinced prescribed assets will become a part of our financial future

Commentary eight
Isaah Mhlanga is their executive chief economist

Isaah Mhlanga
My general sense is it is a very low probability event, it’s unlikely to happen because we have deep capital markets and the capital markets would discipline the state if they came up with policies that are not investor friendly
Devi
Are you saying sleep easy all will be well?
Isaah
I say sleep perhaps with one open the moment it becomes government process then you need to open both eyes, but for now I think it’s a low probability event, but don’t completely discount because its being touted by the ruling party so it has some weight, it’s not a zero percent probability



Commentary nine
But the problem, says Schussler is our government debt to GDP ratio is too high and politicians can’t stop spending.

Devi
We are talking government debt but how would I understand this?
Mike Schussler
Well if my total household earns a R100 rand every year, and I owe R90 every year, that is where South Africa is right now.

Commentary ten
In Schussler’s graph, the red line is our government debt, and the blue line represents that debt plus the debt of state- owned enterprises

MIKE Schussler
Our burden of R90 to R100 is growing every year, and those are the sort of levels economists and ratings agencies will be very worried about

Commentary eleven
And when the coffers run dry, he believes our pension funds will become an easy target.

Mike Schussler
If we have any shock in the financial system in SA and foreigners pull out their money, like they did in the eighties you will have prescribed assets

Commentary twelve
He argues that 36% of government debt is owned by international investors, indicated here in red, and should there be just one more downgrade from Moody’s, those investors who own our debt will be forced to take their money out of our markets

Mike Brown
Now once you lose your investment grade rating a number of those investors are no longer allowed in terms of your mandate to invest in government bonds that don’t have an investment grade rating so there would be a significant outflow of capital from South Africa by those people who hold South African bonds
Devi
And how do we fill that hole?
Mike
By filling it up with South African local investments. Where is the capital to do this, well its sitting in the pension fund industry?

Enoch Godongwana
The only way these people can downgrade us now is if we don’t have a growth story after the elections. If we talk a growth story, Moody’s is not going to downgrade us


Commentary thirteen
The apartheid government also tried unsuccessfully to prescribe assets says Mike Brown

Mike Brown
What happened in the past is that you had to put 65% of your money into government bonds
Devi
Was it as much as that?!
MIKE
As much as that, and the net result was that interest rates doubled to encourage people to invest in the pension funds to invest in government bonds and interest rates went up to 25% at one stage, so the economic impact of having a clumsy approach, could be very dangerous for the economy

DEVI
So, are you guys planning on touching the pension funds, let’s just get down to this?
Enoch Godongwana
Let me just say we have got no intention of touching the pension funds, by the way the issue of prescribed assets is largely pushed by Cosatu than by us. What we are responding to is a call for looking at prescribed assets, in cases where insurances and pension funds are not investing in developmental projects

Commentary fourteen
And the developmental projects, he says need funding right now, are new coal mines.

Enoch Godongwana
Two banks have made a statement, NEDBANK AND STANDARD BANK that they are not going to put money in coal anymore. For me that is an invitation for prescribed assets, because as a country we have sixty-six billion tons of coal

Commentary fifteen
Godongwana didn’t mention coal’s environmental hazards and argued that investors could still make returns from coal if it was run along similar lines to governments renewable IPP programme which is backed by their guarantees.

Enoch
We will definitely look at all financial savings of South Africans that should be utilized not necessarily in assets that are not going to yield returns, because no one has said coal is not profitable. People are saying that coal is dirty, it doesn’t mean that if you put money into coal that you are not going to make returns as you are going to make in renewables.

DEVI:
But fund managers should be allowed to put money wherever they think they will get a good return?



Enoch Godongwana
No, no, no, the question is the following. Who determines policy? A government of the day determines policy, you can’t therefore have an individual determine what is the policy of the country, in other words the country will not utilize coal.

Devi
So, what can I do?
Mike Schussler
We have seen before that people then stopped saving and they looked for other things so in SA we had the strange the second- hand old car market took off, and people were looking at ways to get out by buying gold coins
Devi
What you are going to say stamps next?
Mike
Stamps
Devi
Really?!
I will see you at Checkers on pensioners day
Mike
laughs
Devi
Are we not being alarmist?
Mike
Not at all we have had it before and we still have it today, we have a form of prescribed assets, and all it takes is a signature

Commentary sixteen
Meanwhile all we can do is wait, and hope that sense prevails.

Devi
Can I say something now, look after our pension money well, because for most of us it’s all we have!
Enoch Godongwana
I am older than you. I am more concerned about the pensions than any South Africans. I have not accumulated much, and I am old. That is why we say we will investigate because we want to make sure that if we do it, we know the implication

THE END 12 minutes









PROMO ONE 11 Seconds
Commentary
Will our pension pot become an easy target for an indebted government?
Mike Schussler has crunched the numbers.
Mike
Our pension pot is the sexiest thing for government at the moment.

PROMO TWO 11 seconds
Will a resolution in the ANC manifesto dictate that some of your hard- earned pension savings be invested in assets identified by government? We explore prescribed assets

PROMO THREE 11 seconds
The ANC is adamant that the resolution to prescribe assets will not mean you must invest your pension in State owned enterprises. Instead we could be looking at investing in coal mines.

NAMES

MIKE BROWN
CHAIRMAN: SOCIETY OF INVESTMENT ANALYSTS

ENOCH GODONGWANA
CHAIRMAN: ANC ECONOMIC TRANSFORMATION COMMITTEE

MIKE SCHUSSLER
ECONOMIST

ISAAH MHLANGA
EXECUTIVE CHIEF ECONOMIST ALEXANDER FORBES

2019 Script: FINAL SCRIPT PENSION CAPTURE TX Sunday 5th May 2019. Commentary One Imagine a future where the investment of your pension money is not determined by where you can get the best returns, but rather by a government decree, based on their financial needs. This is called prescribed assets and its proposed in the ANC’s latest manifesto. It says: We will investigate the introduction of prescribed assets on financial institutions’ funds to unlock resources for investments in social and economic development LINK That proposal in the manifesto sent a shiver through the pension fund industry, but perhaps the rest of us didn’t understand how prescribed assets if implemented could devastate the health of our pensions Commentary Two Mike Brown is chairman of the investment analysts society. He also runs his own fund. MIKE BROWN We were concerned about it because don’t forget the ANC is a socialist government and typically, they tend to try lay their hands on as much of other people’s money as they can. Commentary Three At this stage it’s still an ANC resolution, and not yet government policy. Enoch Godongwana is the head of Economic transformation for the party, and was one of the drafters of that resolution Enoch Godongwana The resolution says carefully worded that we want to investigate prescribed assets, that is what the resolution says. The reason we have crafted it in that way, is that we don’t implement without clear thinking, on which asset classes, what are the cost to our economy. Commentary four Already your pension funds are subject to a softer form of prescription called Regulation 28. This compels your fund manager to spread your investment across several asset classes. Right now, that’s a maximum of 75% in the share market, 30% offshore, 25% in listed properties and as much as you wish in government bonds and cash. Enoch Godongwana So for us, we may have to move for an amendment and broadening of regulation 28, if the circumstances after investigation necessitated that Commentary five courtesy GCIS All it would take is a minister’s signature to amend Regulation 28, and overnight you could be forced to invest in government assets that may offer little or no return Mike Brown Government can change that regulation, it doesn’t need an act of parliament. A regulation can out from the minister of finance can say well now you have to have a much bigger percentage in government bonds. In other words, you must fund the government. Devi There is something that is not right about that. I mean morally right Mike Brown I don’t think its correct at all! This is just state capture in its next form and hopefully we can stop it happening. Commentary six Many of us are not aware that South Africa has one of the biggest pension savings in the world in dollar terms. Economist Mike Schussler has done the research and his numbers show over four trillion rands sitting in our collective pension savings Mike Schussler South Africa is the emerging market which has the highest amount of pension assets in the world. There is no emerging market, including China, including Brazil, including Russia that has anywhere close to the savings that South Africa has! South Africa has more pension funds savings than either France or Germany! Devi Is that the reason why our pension pot is so sexy because there is all this money sitting there? Mike Our pension pot is the sexiest thing for government at the moment. I really think it is likely to happen Devi That would be very worrying because I wouldn’t want someone to tell me where to put my money Mike Exactly, and your money will not grow as quickly as it should, and you will end up a very poor person if the returns aren’t right. For example, if people told you told to put your money in Eskom Bonds and Eskom cannot pay back Devi Not on your life and then what! Mike And then you will live in your kids garage if you are old. Commentary seven But Enoch Godongwana dismisses this interpretation of their resolution as nonsense. Enoch So, you are singling out, deliberately in my view a scarecrow, that the only way we can do prescribed assets is to send it to an SOE, that is not what we are talking about! Devi But you are not categorically saying to me that won’t happen? Enoch Godongwana I said it won’t happen! Devi Guaranteed? Enoch Godongwana Guaranteed. It won’t happen DEVI Do you blame people for not having trust right now? They don’t trust…. Enoch I don’t expect people to trust in the environment in which Eskom has performed. But I don’t expect when you talk about prescribed assets, of necessity, you mean we put them in SAA that is not what we are talking about! Devi The point I am making is that I don’t trust… ENOCH You are not the one who is going to make the decision about prescribed assets Devi No I am not, that is for sure! Enoch Then you should be listening to me I am the one who is going to make that decision about prescribed assets LINK But Alexander Forbes, who manage one of South Africa’s largest pension funds, is not convinced prescribed assets will become a part of our financial future Commentary eight Isaah Mhlanga is their executive chief economist Isaah Mhlanga My general sense is it is a very low probability event, it’s unlikely to happen because we have deep capital markets and the capital markets would discipline the state if they came up with policies that are not investor friendly Devi Are you saying sleep easy all will be well? Isaah I say sleep perhaps with one open the moment it becomes government process then you need to open both eyes, but for now I think it’s a low probability event, but don’t completely discount because its being touted by the ruling party so it has some weight, it’s not a zero percent probability Commentary nine But the problem, says Schussler is our government debt to GDP ratio is too high and politicians can’t stop spending. Devi We are talking government debt but how would I understand this? Mike Schussler Well if my total household earns a R100 rand every year, and I owe R90 every year, that is where South Africa is right now. Commentary ten In Schussler’s graph, the red line is our government debt, and the blue line represents that debt plus the debt of state- owned enterprises MIKE Schussler Our burden of R90 to R100 is growing every year, and those are the sort of levels economists and ratings agencies will be very worried about Commentary eleven And when the coffers run dry, he believes our pension funds will become an easy target. Mike Schussler If we have any shock in the financial system in SA and foreigners pull out their money, like they did in the eighties you will have prescribed assets Commentary twelve He argues that 36% of government debt is owned by international investors, indicated here in red, and should there be just one more downgrade from Moody’s, those investors who own our debt will be forced to take their money out of our markets Mike Brown Now once you lose your investment grade rating a number of those investors are no longer allowed in terms of your mandate to invest in government bonds that don’t have an investment grade rating so there would be a significant outflow of capital from South Africa by those people who hold South African bonds Devi And how do we fill that hole? Mike By filling it up with South African local investments. Where is the capital to do this, well its sitting in the pension fund industry? Enoch Godongwana The only way these people can downgrade us now is if we don’t have a growth story after the elections. If we talk a growth story, Moody’s is not going to downgrade us Commentary thirteen The apartheid government also tried unsuccessfully to prescribe assets says Mike Brown Mike Brown What happened in the past is that you had to put 65% of your money into government bonds Devi Was it as much as that?! MIKE As much as that, and the net result was that interest rates doubled to encourage people to invest in the pension funds to invest in government bonds and interest rates went up to 25% at one stage, so the economic impact of having a clumsy approach, could be very dangerous for the economy DEVI So, are you guys planning on touching the pension funds, let’s just get down to this? Enoch Godongwana Let me just say we have got no intention of touching the pension funds, by the way the issue of prescribed assets is largely pushed by Cosatu than by us. What we are responding to is a call for looking at prescribed assets, in cases where insurances and pension funds are not investing in developmental projects Commentary fourteen And the developmental projects, he says need funding right now, are new coal mines. Enoch Godongwana Two banks have made a statement, NEDBANK AND STANDARD BANK that they are not going to put money in coal anymore. For me that is an invitation for prescribed assets, because as a country we have sixty-six billion tons of coal Commentary fifteen Godongwana didn’t mention coal’s environmental hazards and argued that investors could still make returns from coal if it was run along similar lines to governments renewable IPP programme which is backed by their guarantees. Enoch We will definitely look at all financial savings of South Africans that should be utilized not necessarily in assets that are not going to yield returns, because no one has said coal is not profitable. People are saying that coal is dirty, it doesn’t mean that if you put money into coal that you are not going to make returns as you are going to make in renewables. DEVI: But fund managers should be allowed to put money wherever they think they will get a good return? Enoch Godongwana No, no, no, the question is the following. Who determines policy? A government of the day determines policy, you can’t therefore have an individual determine what is the policy of the country, in other words the country will not utilize coal. Devi So, what can I do? Mike Schussler We have seen before that people then stopped saving and they looked for other things so in SA we had the strange the second- hand old car market took off, and people were looking at ways to get out by buying gold coins Devi What you are going to say stamps next? Mike Stamps Devi Really?! I will see you at Checkers on pensioners day Mike laughs Devi Are we not being alarmist? Mike Not at all we have had it before and we still have it today, we have a form of prescribed assets, and all it takes is a signature Commentary sixteen Meanwhile all we can do is wait, and hope that sense prevails. Devi Can I say something now, look after our pension money well, because for most of us it’s all we have! Enoch Godongwana I am older than you. I am more concerned about the pensions than any South Africans. I have not accumulated much, and I am old. That is why we say we will investigate because we want to make sure that if we do it, we know the implication THE END 12 minutes PROMO ONE 11 Seconds Commentary Will our pension pot become an easy target for an indebted government? Mike Schussler has crunched the numbers. Mike Our pension pot is the sexiest thing for government at the moment. PROMO TWO 11 seconds Will a resolution in the ANC manifesto dictate that some of your hard- earned pension savings be invested in assets identified by government? We explore prescribed assets PROMO THREE 11 seconds The ANC is adamant that the resolution to prescribe assets will not mean you must invest your pension in State owned enterprises. Instead we could be looking at investing in coal mines. metadata.Further information: By 2021 South Africa will be R3.5 trillion rand in debt. We are not far off from that right now. Take a look at South Africa’s debt clock run by commodity.com, every second our interest compounding at eye watering figures, faster than one can say Tito Mboweni. Our interest payments alone cost over R5000 every second, and currently national debt per citizen sits at around R56 000. In economists speak, our debt is around 56% of GDP. Treasury have not minced their words and things may only stabilize around 5- 6 years from now at 57% of GDP. The above data shows that this year alone R202 billion rand of our hard- earned money will go just into servicing our debt. It’s a frightening picture because South Africa is broke, and government is struggling to find money to pay its debts. But they have a plan and that plan could directly impact on the money you are saving for your retirement. ENTER PRESCRIBED ASETTS In January this year when the ANC presented their Manifesto, they said the following: “We will investigate the introduction of prescribed assets on financial institutions funds to unlock resources for investment in social and economic development” BUT WHAT EXACTLY DOES THAT MEAN? In a nutshell, it means that when government needs money, (which they do) all they have to do is make it mandatory for fund managers managing any of your savings, to place a percentage of those savings into funds identified by government. In other words, failing State owned assets like Eskom or SAA. Neither you nor your fund manager will have any choice on the matter, and this could have a devastating impact on your pension. THE HONEY POT While South Africa may be broke, there is still a large honey pot that till now has been left untouched. Collectively South Africans have R4.3 trillion rand in private pension funds. What is incredible is that we have more in our pension funds than Germany, for example, and are up there with some of the first world countries. This huge pot of money has not gone unnoticed by the ANC. According to economist Mike Schussler whose recent study sounds a dire warning, it will be a lot easier for the government to raid these funds than go to the IMF cap in hand. The IMF will demand transparency and reform, but prescribing assets can be done without even passing new laws. All they need to do is amend regulation 28. REGULATION 28 Right now, Regulation 28 is there to protect you. It ensures that a fund manager spreads your risk – he can only put 75% of your pension into equities, 25% into local or international property and 30% into foreign investments. But the catch, according to Mike Schussler is that regulation 28 means that should government want to prescribe that your pension goes into a loss- making hole, they don’t even have to change the law, all they need to do is amend regulation 28. ITS BEEN DONE BEFORE When the apartheid government was the pariah of the world, they struggled to get access to international finance and forced pension funds to invest in SASOL, ISCOR and various other entities, but abandoned the policy in 1989. WHO WILL IT AFFECT? About 11 to 16 million South Africans with pension funds and more if one considers the knock on effect, and according to Schussler’s graphs – it’s mostly black South Africans whose investment in pension funds has increased dramatically, while white pension fund investors have dropped from 70% down to 22%. Coloured and Indian investors have stayed more or less constant. WHAT EFFECT WILL PRESCRIBING ASETTS HAVE? Disastrous according to ALF Lees and various other pension fund managers, including economist Thabi Leoka. They say money will pour out of this country. Not so says Mark Barnes, CEO of the post office. BROKEN PROMISES The debt burden is huge – add the debts from State owned enterprises and a debt of closer to 100% of GDP is the real story. In 2008 it was 46% of GDP – 11 years later its practically double – and don’t listen to the promises of politicians warns Schussler. They told us that SA will not have a debt to GDP ratio of more than 40%. Oh dear that didn’t last, so the next line in the sand they drew was 50%. Then 60% …oops, we crossed that line too…so what next FALLING OUT OF THE WORLD BOND INDICES If that sounds complicated it really isn’t, but one does need to understand how that can impact on you. Currently foreign investors make up nearly 40% of our debt market. But if we continue to mismanage our economy we will most certainly get downgraded again. And there is a limit to these downgrades. At a point portfolio managers will be forced to withdraw their funds that is propping up our debt. That will make our debt more expensive and government will need to issue further bonds and then all they have to do is change the % share of regulation 28 and force fund managers to buy up those bonds. That is the picture Schussler is warning us against. SO WHAT IS EVERYONE ELSE SAYING? After the ANC issued its manifesto in January, the pension fund industry was skrikked, but two things happened. An election was announced, and the ANC went silent on the matter. And because there were no further details available, the pension fund industry appeared to stop panicking. In fact, Alexander Forbes chief Economist Isaah Mahlanga said his view was that it was a low probability event. Not so fast, warns ALF LEES, the DA shadow deputy minister who sits on the finance committee in parliament with the ANC. He is convinced that it will come into effect at some point after the elections. Surprisingly the unions are apparently in favour of prescribed assets. WHAT IS THE PLAN? There are at least two people in the ruling party who should know – Yunus Carrim chairperson of the finance committee and Enoch Godongwana, head of the ANC economic transformation committee. We will endeavor to get answers from either of these politicians. Let us not forget that Carrim is a communist so nationalizing your pension is not novel to him, it’s just the way he rolls. SO WHAT DO YOU DO? Don’t panic say the experts. We will explore in more detail what options are available to investors should prescribed assets become a reality IS IT CRUNCH TIME? Yes says Schussler.
